newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - June 5.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company DAILY
TELEGRAPH
-- OFWAT THREATENS WATER DIVIDENDS

Water regulator Ian Byatt was ringing for the last orders on water companies who pay unsustainable' dividends. Byatt warned that these companies faced tougher treatment at the next regulatory pricing review. A spokesman for the Water regulator said that any company deemed to be paying excessive dividends will be written back into the companies' balance sheet' and taken into account at the next periodic review.
--SOUTHERN ELECTRIC PLANNING FURTHER RETURN TO HOLDERS

Southern Electric, the last regional electricity company, is planning to return more money to its shareholders after the budget; this coming hard on the heels of a 156 million stg handout and share restructuring four months ago. The company said the level of payout would depend on the size of the windfall tax. Analysts said unless the windfall tax is unduly harsh then the payout will be well in excess of 100 million stg.
-- BRITISH ENERGY TURNS IN PROFIT

British Energy announced its first profits level since floating on the stock market. Last year the company has pre-tax profit of 61 million stg compared with a 155 million loss the previous year. British Energy also announced a deal with British Nuclear Fuels that will cap its spent fuel liabilities. British Energy's chief executive said the extension of an earlier agreement with BNFL from 200 to 2006 will save British Energy 10 million stg in fuel costs this year.
THE TIMES
-- MIRROR PLANS VEHICLE TO PROVIDE CABLE TV PACKAGES

The Mirror Group is planning to launch a company, known internally as the Programme Company, that would provide TV programming packages to cable companies in competition with those offered by satellite broadcaster BSkyB. The company would also attempt to create a brand that is clearly identified with cable TV and provide marketing services. The Mirror Group is in talks with Flextech, the cable and satellite programmer, about joining the venture.
-- PRU CHIEF TO CAPTAIN WELFARE-TO-WORK TEAM

Chairman of insurance group Prudential Corporation, Peter Davis, is to head a task force overseeing Labour's welfare-to-work programme. This comes as Prudential announced it will spend millions of stg to toughen up proficiency tests for all 5,500 direct sales staff after its training and compliance standards were criticised by the Securities and Investments Board, the chief City watchdog.
-- DAVIS TALKS OF EMU RISKS

Deputy governor of the Bank of England and soon-to-be head of a stronger Securities and Investments Board, Howard Davis, has said that City firms risked heavy losses if they made the wrong assumptions over the future of monetary union. He called on them to "understand the rigourous stress testing of their portfolios" to ensure they were not dangerously exposed. He said that over the past 18 months bond traders had increasingly based deals on calculations involving the convergence criteria for monetary union and now banks should reassess their positions in the market.
THE GUARDIAN
-- GEORGE TELLS OF HIS FEARS ABOUT A BUYING SPREE

The Governor of the Bank of England, Eddie George, made the chances of an interest rates rise more likely with his increasing fears of a high-street spending boom as a result of the shareout from windfall payouts. Governor's thoughts came on Wednesday as the Bank of England begins to take on its new role of independent operational control over base rates. Governor George warned that the demand from building society and insurance conversions would be significant.
-- COSTLY LESSON FOR THE PRU

The Securities and Investments Board has asked Prudential Corp, the country's biggest insurer, to retest its entire sales force after the watchdog uncovered shortcomings in the firm's training and compliance procedures. Some 5,500 sales staff will be sent back to the classroom for two to three days in the summer so that they can be re-examined on specific investment products.
-- NEW MOOD BRINGS SOCIAL PARTNERSHIP OUT OF THE CLOSET

For many years with the previous Conservative administration social partnership between business, trade unions and government was seen as the 'devil incarnate'. The Trades Union Council's general secretary, John Monks, argues that he is optimistic that the Labour Government's clear commitment and strong mandate means that there is a strong backdrop for constructive dialogue between the Confederation of British Industry and the TUC on a range of issues. The range of issues could include objectives on growth, employment and investment.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BT BONUS LIMIT DOUBLES TO 100 PERCENT OF PAY

British Telecom's annual report shows that senior directors are set to share in the company's package of bonuses since privatisation. Chief executive Peter Bonfield could receive a total payout of four million stg. The bonus schemes represent BT's move to put the pay of British executives on par with their counterparts in the US long-distance operator MCI, which BT is in the process of buying.
-- NFC AXES UP TO 600 JOBS IN FURTHER SHAKE-UP

The transport group which has been restructuring itself for over three years, NFC, has announced a new reorganisation and disposal programme to raise 207 million stg and see the loss of 600 jobs. Chairman Christopher Bland said the restructuring would be the last and would include a 49 million stg exceptional charge in the full year results. He said NFC had achieved significant earnings growth while disposing of two big businesses where the group did not think it had a future.
-- BECKETT OUTLINES PLANS TO BOOST COMPETITIVENESS

President of the Board of Trade, Margaret Beckett, has pledged to continue leaving competitiveness as a primary consideration when vetting takeovers and mergers. She rejected proposals to reverse the burden of proof in merger cases to force a bidder to prove that a takeover was in the public interest and said Labour would not merge the Office of Fair Trading and the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
